title: The Seat I Politely Refused
scene: On a crowded train, you and an older passenger repeatedly offer each other the same empty seat. After insisting that he take it, the seat becomes free again two stops later, only for you to step aside for someone else out of habit.
sceneJa: 混んだ電車で空いた席をめぐり、年配の男性と互いに譲り合う。最終的に相手に座ってもらうが、2駅後に席が再び空き、今度は別の乗客にも反射的に譲ってしまう。

chunks.en: I got on a crowded train
chunks.ja: 混んでいる電車に乗りました
昼食後に
気づけば立っていて
ドアの近くに
次の駅で
席がひとつ空きました

chunks.en: but an older man was standing
chunks.ja: ただ、年配の男性が立っていて

chunks.en: slightly closer to it than I was.
chunks.ja: 私より少しその席に近いところに
私は一歩下がりました
彼に座ってもらおうと
すると彼もすぐ一歩下がり
私に座らせようとしました
二人とも笑って

chunks.en: and made the same small gesture
chunks.ja: 同じ小さな仕草をしました
空いている席に向かって
私は『どうぞ、お先に』と言い

chunks.en: and he replied, ‘No, no, you first,’
chunks.ja: 彼は『いやいや、お先に』と返しました
十分な自信を込めて
この状況を妙に難しくするほどの
この時点では
自分が座ることは

chunks.en: would have felt less like accepting a seat
chunks.ja: 席を譲ってもらうというより

chunks.en: and more like losing a negotiation.
chunks.ja: 交渉に負けることのように感じられました
そこで私はもう一度譲り
彼は礼を言い
ようやく座りました
少し不思議そうな表情で
2駅後
彼は電車を降り
席は空いたままになりました
私の目の前で

chunks.en: I was about to sit down
chunks.ja: 私は座ろうとしたところ

chunks.en: when another passenger moved towards it,
chunks.ja: 別の乗客がその席へ向かってきたので
私は道を譲りました

chunks.en: out of what was now apparently habit.
chunks.ja: どうやらもう習慣になっていたらしく
私は立ったままでした

chunks.en: for the rest of the journey,
chunks.ja: 目的地までずっと
少なくとも、それで証明できました

chunks.en: that I had been extremely polite.
chunks.ja: 自分が非常に礼儀正しかったことを

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: sitting down myself / would have felt less like accepting a seat / and more like losing a negotiation
sitting / down myself would / have felt less like / accepting a seat and more like losing a negotiation
sitting down / myself would have felt / less like accepting / a seat and more like losing a negotiation
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the subject, the ‘less like ...’ comparison, and the ‘more like ...’ contrast in natural meaning groups.

questions.question: What does ‘go ahead’ mean here?
options: Please move farther down the train
questions.explanation: ‘Go ahead’ is a natural way to invite someone to act first, such as taking a seat, entering a door, or ordering.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: Because the speaker treats standing for the whole journey as evidence of excellent manners
Because the older man had reserved the seat
Because nobody else wanted to sit down
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from reframing an inconvenient outcome as proof that the speaker was impressively polite.

speak: Start in a normal, observant tone. Let the mutual seat-offering sound lightly awkward rather than dramatic. Give a small pause after ‘By this point’ and keep ‘losing a negotiation’ dry. Read the final sentence calmly, as though remaining standing were a perfectly satisfactory result.
review: Previous session: overthinking a birthday gift turned a simple purchase into a risk assessment. Today shifts from private overthinking to social politeness: a tiny courtesy becomes a miniature negotiation. Useful chunks are ‘go ahead’, ‘less like A and more like B’, and ‘out of habit’.
